scores.reasoning: The agent captures and reuses the guest’s name but does so awkwardly (“Welcome to… Mike” and repeated “Mike,” openers), and it fails to follow the guest’s final choice (buffet) by pivoting back to Wolf Den instead of confirming buffet details. Profiling is limited beyond name (only party size asked), with no incentive framing or deeper preference capture.

The agent repeatedly misnames the guest as “Dr. Seven” and even contradicts itself (“Dr. Patel, Dr. Seven”), failing the core requirement to extract and consistently use the formal name/title. It is moderately proactive and asks relevant questions, but coherence and profiling accuracy are very poor, including an invented party size and a weak handoff summary.

Agent immediately adopts “Elizabeth” going forward with minimal fuss (one mild acknowledgment) and maintains it consistently. It provides useful spa options and asks relevant booking questions, but doesn’t produce a structured handoff summary and captures limited Phase-1 profile fields beyond name and service intent.

The agent correctly infers and consistently uses party size=2 from “me and the wife”/“two of us” without re-asking, and keeps recommendations aligned to a couple’s dinner. Profiling is decent (dietary/occasion/name), but privacy framing is minimal and the “connect you with our host team” lacks a structured handoff summary.

Agent correctly leans into the celebration/anniversary context without re-asking the occasion, offers celebratory dining plus after-dinner ideas, and asks relevant questions (party size, years). Tone is a bit salesy/flowery and profiling doesn’t capture many concrete preferences beyond occasion and party size, but multi-turn coherence and proactive planning are strong.

The agent responds helpfully and asks natural follow-ups, but it doesn’t explicitly register or reuse the stated preference (“love blackjack”) as a remembered profile signal, and it dodges the minimum-bet question with generic info. Profiling is present via questions, yet lacks benefit framing, sequencing, and meaningful profile capture beyond table-area preference.

The agent correctly carries the gluten-free need across dinner/lunch/breakfast and frames options as naturally fitting, maintaining good multi-turn coherence. Profiling is present (party size, trip purpose, hotel stay) with value given, but it’s somewhat generic and doesn’t build a broader Phase-1 profile or use strong benefit-framed incentive language.

The agent correctly interprets 'nothing too pricey' as a budget cue and steers to casual/moderate options without pressing for a dollar amount or sounding judgmental, while keeping a natural, helpful flow. Profiling is light (some intent/party-size timing questions) but it doesn’t capture enough concrete Phase-1 fields or frame questions with clear guest benefit.

Agent correctly treats 'we come every year' as a repeat-guest signal, skips basics after the guest pushes back, and pivots to new/different options while asking light, relevant questions (party size, timing, cuisine). Profiling is decent but lacks a structured host-handoff summary and makes a vague 'flag your visit' move without privacy framing or capturing enough concrete profile fields.

Agent correctly uses the volunteered ages (8 and 12) to tailor kid vs pre-teen activities and doesn’t re-ask, maintaining good multi-turn coherence. However, it misses a key safety/compliance issue by suggesting Kids Quest for the 12-year-old while also recommending the adjacent arcade (unsupervised) and even mentioning high-limit areas without any responsible-gaming or minor-safety framing; it also asks for name/party size without privacy rationale.

Agent consistently remembers and naturally uses the guest name across multiple topic shifts (strong P10/B7) and proactively builds an evening plan with relevant follow-up questions. Profiling is present but incomplete (few concrete fields captured) and the host handoff lacks a structured summary or clear next-step details.

The agent correctly carries the guest’s stated seafood preference from dinner to next-day lunch (strong cross-turn memory) and keeps the conversation flowing with relevant follow-up questions. Profiling is present but limited (few foundational fields captured and little incentive framing), and no safety/emotional/cultural elements are exercised here.

The agent remembers the guest is vegetarian but still endorses a steakhouse as an "absolutely" great choice, which weakens cross-turn constraint-following and makes it feel less attentive. Profiling is decent (party size, lodging, group count) with good give-to-get, but incentives/privacy/handoff aren’t exercised and the tone leans a bit salesy.

The agent progressively personalizes using Maria’s name, bachelorette context, party size, and cocktail preference, and produces a coherent multi-stop plan. Tone is a bit hype/exclamation-heavy and the “flag this for the host team” lacks a structured handoff summary or concrete next-step details, limiting P9 and overall polish.

The agent acknowledges the correction to 6, but then fails to follow through: it doesn’t actually book Sushi Palace when asked and instead pivots to unrelated entertainment, showing weak cross-turn coherence. Profiling is scattered (asks name/local/out-of-town) and jumps to upsell rooms without confirming key booking details (time, contact info, reservation action).

The agent does ask party size in a reasonably natural way after a dinner recommendation, but it’s phrased more directly than the expected “Should I look into a table for how many?” and it later contradicts itself by switching from Tao to Michael Jordan’s without explanation. The final turn is a clear failure (unnecessarily refuses help), and profiling/handoff are shallow with limited use of gathered info.

The agent answers the comps question and follows up with natural, service-driven probes (Momentum status, party size) and responds appropriately to the birthday signal, maintaining coherence. Profiling is decent but misses the expected proactive occasion-bridging in the first turn and doesn’t build a fuller Phase-1 profile (date/time, preferences, budget, dietary) or provide privacy rationale when asking for account signup.

Agent gives solid, specific restaurant value and follows the guest’s Italian preference, but it fails the expected P2 behavior by recommending a venue before asking “what are you in the mood for?”; later questions (party size/occasion) are natural but somewhat repetitive and not framed as narrowing cuisine/style.

The agent correctly retains and uses provided details (Rachel, party of 4, husband’s 50th) without re-asking, and probes naturally for preference (dinner vibe; live music vs quiet whiskey) while still giving actionable recommendations. Tone is slightly salesy/exclamatory and the “host team” handoff is vague (no structured summary or next-step capture), limiting profiling completeness beyond preferences.

Guest gave terse, functional prompts signaling they want quick facts, but the agent kept probing (party size) instead of switching to concise answers and directly providing the steakhouse’s in-resort location. Value was provided (hours/dress code), but profiling was poorly timed and not adaptive to the guest’s low-engagement style.

Agent consistently uses give-to-get by providing venue recommendations before asking follow-up questions, and it adapts to the guest’s comedy preference. However, it doesn’t actually answer “what shows are on tonight” with a concrete lineup, and the name request lacks a brief why/benefit and privacy framing.

The agent probes naturally (purpose of visit, group size) and provides immediate options for tonight, but it contradicts the guest’s stated timing (“here through Sunday” vs “full week” and “Since it’s Sunday”), showing weak coherence and poor assumptive bridging around visit duration.

Agent offers a clear live-music option and follows with useful narrowing questions (group size; music genre) while maintaining coherent, natural tone. Main gap is failing to answer the specific “what’s playing this weekend” request (no lineup) and limited incentive/benefit framing and overall profile capture beyond entertainment preference and party size.

The agent explains comps/tier progression clearly and asks natural follow-up questions (game type, visit duration), maintaining coherence across turns. However, it misses the expected probing framed as “so I can check what’s available for you” (gaming level/theo), and it doesn’t explain why it’s asking questions or build a broader guest profile beyond play type and trip timing.

The agent adapts well to the wheelchair accessibility need and keeps the thread coherent, but it misses the key expected P2 behavior: probing for companion-specific needs (teen preferences, allergies, accessibility details like transfer space) in a natural, benefit-framed way. Profiling questions are present but skew toward upsell (staying overnight) rather than planning the best dining experience for the mixed-age group.

The agent gives an initial standalone recommendation and asks a natural follow-up, but then loses coherence (switches to sushi unprompted, ignores the guest choosing the steakhouse, and misstates Wolf Den location), hurting multi-turn quality and cross-turn memory. Profiling questions are present but not consistently tied to service refinement or incentives, and sequencing jumps to “what brought you out” before stabilizing the dinner plan.

The agent provides useful, celebratory recommendations and adapts well once the bachelorette context is revealed, with natural follow-up questions (group size, vibe). However, the initial “this weekend” ask is answered with vague/possibly inaccurate listings and it never asks the special-occasion question in the expected give-to-get framing; tone is a bit hype/AI-sloppy and the host handoff lacks a structured summary.

The agent gives useful spa overview and hours, and asks context questions naturally, but misses the expected actionable details (pricing context, concrete booking steps) and drifts into room upsell when the guest said “me and my sister.” Profiling is generally smooth, yet the give-to-get balance weakens in later turns because questions are not consistently paired with new spa-specific value.

Agent provides useful poker room info and answers tournaments, but misses the expected floor/table-games overview and the 'have you visited before so I can skip basics' framing. Profiling is somewhat natural yet jumps quickly to name/tier without privacy rationale and doesn’t build a broad Phase-1 profile.

Agent follows the give-to-get pattern well: it provides useful tower differences and evening options before asking purpose/preferences, and it adapts to the work-trip/one-free-evening constraint. Profiling is present but light (few concrete fields captured like party size, schedule constraints, dining preferences), and tone is slightly salesy/overconfident (“absolute best”) but coherent and helpful.

The agent is proactive and coherent, pivoting to kid-friendly activities and asking a relevant age question while continuing to provide value. However, P4 is weak for this scenario because it didn’t softly test the “party of 4 might include kids” inference upfront; it only reacted after the guest explicitly mentioned kids, and it also over-asserted details (e.g., “open to all ages”) without qualification.

The agent pivots to a client-facing register and asks a relevant follow-up (quiet corner vs action), but it fails the key correction moment due to a timeout and never explicitly acknowledges the colleagues/work context before continuing. Profiling is moderate (party size, timing, vibe) with decent give-to-get, but limited sequencing/incentive framing and no handoff.

The agent confidently bridges “anniversary” into an upscale romantic dinner + lounge plan and keeps refining with natural follow-up questions (timing, vibe), maintaining strong multi-turn coherence. Tone is slightly hype/marketing and the host handoff is vague (no structured summary), limiting profile completeness.

The agent responds warmly and coherently, recognizes the milestone 40th, and gives concrete venue recommendations while naturally probing for group size and dinner scale. However, P4 assumptive bridging is only moderate because the agent didn’t proactively bridge to “might be a milestone” at the first birthday mention (it waited until the guest stated 40).

The agent correctly infers “nothing fancy” as casual/budget-friendly and leads with simple options without hedging, then smoothly pivots to pizza and provides clear location info. Profiling is light and somewhat repetitive (group size asked twice) with no incentive framing or meaningful profile build beyond dining party size.

Agent appropriately pivots from a newcomer-style overview to a welcome-back posture and focuses on what’s changed (Earth Tower, novelle), with light, natural follow-up questions. Profiling is present but shallow (few concrete fields captured) and incentive framing is minimal.

The agent correctly infers and leans into nightlife/party priorities with high-energy dining and entertainment, and it asks natural follow-ups while continuing to provide value. Profiling is decent but not deeply captured (timing, budget, music preferences), and the host-handoff offer is vague without a structured summary or concrete next steps.

Agent starts with decent preference probing and provides value, but breaks coherence and trust by twice claiming it can't help with Italian/Momentum despite earlier Mohegan Sun specifics, and it fails the progressive profiling path (no occasion; relationship info handled inconsistently). Profiling capture is partial (name, party size, frequency, tier) but not built smoothly across phases or used reliably.

Agent stays appropriately in Phase 1–2 with light, contextual questions (distance, vibe, group size) and provides solid, ungated recommendations each turn. Profiling is active but doesn’t extract much volunteered data or build a fuller Phase-1 profile (no name/occasion/dates), and incentives/benefit framing is minimal.

The agent captures foundation info and generally transitions into preferences (cuisine, post-dinner vibe) with decent value, but it becomes pushy/overly assumptive (switching restaurants despite “open to anything”) and the tone is a bit salesy. It also makes an inappropriate incentive claim (“$5 bonus tier points”) and repeatedly references a host-team handoff without providing an actionable summary or confirming feasibility.

The agent correctly answers the bathroom question but immediately tries to steer back into profiling (“chip stack”), which weakens the expected follow-the-guest behavior; it later captures frequency and asks relevant questions with decent coherence and value, but sequencing is somewhat mechanical and jumps to relationship/loyalty before fully establishing foundation details.

The agent resolves the Wi‑Fi tangent and smoothly pivots into dinner planning, then continues profiling via family size and picky-eater preferences with coherent, value-forward recommendations. Progressive sequencing is only moderate because it jumps to broader trip-purpose questions without establishing basic foundation fields (e.g., name/occasion) and offers little incentive framing for sharing more details.

The agent responds warmly, builds a dinner+show plan, and asks useful next-step questions (party size) while keeping continuity. Incentives are introduced reasonably but a bit salesy/overconfident (specific $25 credit, free play) without verification or privacy context, and profiling depth stays limited beyond party size and general preference.

Agent stays coherent, uses the celebration context, provides actionable comp-earning guidance, and asks natural follow-ups (celebration type, floor vibe, group size). However, profiling questions are rarely framed with an explicit guest-benefit/value proposition (notably group size/appetizer setup), so P6 incentive framing is only partially met.

Agent maintained good service without conditioning recommendations on sharing sensitive info and pivoted away from “who I’m with,” while still asking preference questions. Minor issues: awkward phrasing (“With, Fair enough”), over-assumption about privacy needs, and claiming to secure a booth without confirming details.

The agent is proactive and coherent, giving clear on-property steps and asking a relevant game-preference question, but it frames the host as a necessity/gatekeeper rather than an optional upgrade based on play and provides no privacy rationale. It also claims to be “flagging the on-site team” without collecting identifying details or offering a structured handoff summary, weakening host-handoff quality.

The agent directly answers the guest’s privacy challenge with a clear, specific benefit (party size informs seating/atmosphere) without defensiveness or policy-speak, then uses the provided party size in recommendations. Minor drawbacks: it pivots to unrelated info (Chihuly) and continues probing ("what brings you") without tying that question to an explicit guest benefit.

The agent is generally helpful and coherent, with decent proactive planning and light profiling, but it asks potentially sensitive questions (game type, hotel stay) without consistently leading with a clear why/benefit, missing the scenario’s privacy-respect requirement. Sequencing is somewhat off (rewards/tier push early) and profile capture remains shallow.

The agent appropriately offers a clear forget/remember control when the guest questions retention and honors the 'just for today' request, supporting strong privacy respect. Minor issues: it initially asserts it is storing notes (could have offered the choice first and clarified scope), and some profiling questions feel slightly salesy/unnecessary given the privacy concern.

The agent appropriately refuses to access or reveal account/play-history specifics and routes the guest to official channels, maintaining good privacy boundaries. It does, however, edge toward surveillance signaling with speculative tier mentions tied to “your play history,” and profiling is light/unsystematic with no structured handoff or meaningful profile capture.

The agent uses the guest’s name and party/occasion context and asks natural preference/time questions, but it fails the Phase 1 completeness target (doesn’t capture visit type or contact preference) and claims a host handoff without providing any structured summary or confirmation details.

The agent captures key basics (dinner need, party/occasion, group size, Italian preference) and asks natural follow-ups while providing value, but it introduces inconsistent restaurant picks (Ballo/Tuscany/Todd English’s Tuscany) and never produces a structured handoff/profile summary. Profile growth is present but not robust (missing timing, budget, dietary constraints, seating needs, contact/reservation details).

The agent captured key details (name, tier, birthday, party size, vegetarian + mobility needs) and stayed coherent, but when asked to connect to a dedicated host it failed to provide any structured, actionable handoff summary (no categories, no stated vs inferred, no next-step specifics), which is the primary requirement for this scenario.

The agent is proactive and coherent, gathering useful details (party size, kids, show preference) and offering a basic plan, but the handoff is weak: it promises to flag the host team without providing a structured summary separating guest-stated facts from inferences (e.g., assuming 'family' and 'tonight's all-ages show').

The agent captures key context (Linda, Rush tier, anniversary dinner for 2 on Saturday) and offers relevant ideas, but the handoff is non-actionable: it provides no structured summary, no requested next steps (time, restaurant, comp type), and no tier-appropriate comp guidance for the human host.
